name: p70_replication
question: Under a fair external predictive-codelength benchmark, does the published P70 four-slot factorization generalize better than predeclared alternative segmentations, and can its structural values be independently reproduced?

upstream.spec_layer_B: p70_rules_canonical.json section-weighted 210 rules (not reconstructible) — NOT implemented; optional fixed external input only
upstream.their_target_rejected: grammar's own entropy profile total 10.311 bits; zero residual is an identity, not evidence
upstream.transcription_version: P70 used ZL_ivtff_2b; our corpus is ZL3b-n (3b) => reproduction approximate only

prospectivity: NON-PROSPECTIVE: P70 was built on the whole VMS; the E007 folio split is only a common predictive comparison surface, not evidence P70 was unseen.

p70_spec.parse: longest-match prefix -> gallows -> suffix(from end) -> core=remainder; ch/sh are prefixes; degenerate fallback = whole token in core

primary_objective: prequential (online) KT predictive description length, bits/surface-token, identical estimator + char-level escape for all models; lower = better generalization
token_population: strict tokens (non-uncertain), running text only; identical for all models

split.note: domain-separated from E006; primary metric is prequential and split-free, split used for secondary held-out arm and 5-fold stability

decision_gate: STRUCTURAL_SUPPORT iff coverage>=99% AND P70 beats A0 by >=0.05 bits/token AND beats every non-deferred competitor by >=0.05 bits/token or is lowest in >=4/5 folds AND not a complexity/fallback artefact AND lowest in both Currier A and B; else REPRODUCED_BUT_NOT_VALIDATED / REPRODUCTION_FAILURE / SPECIFICATION_AMBIGUITY
claim_ceiling: Reproducible four-slot structural factorization that generalizes better than tested alternatives; NOT morphemes/language/decipherment.
enriched_records_policy: never training labels or gold; optional published-reference-output cross-check only after our parser is frozen
